paper.title: Polynomial-time Algorithms for Multiple-arm Identification with Full-bandit Feedback

unmapped: Super-arms are all size-k subsets of n base arms (K = n choose k); only the sum of rewards of the pulled super-arm is observed (full-bandit)
Per-arm noise bounded in [-R, R] with R known (noise of sum bounded by kR)
Static (non-adaptive) allocation strategy p given as input
settings.definition_quote: she can only observe the sum of rewards $r_{M_t}= \theta(M_t)+\sum_{e \in M_t}\epsilon_t(e)$ at each pull ... ${ \cal M}= \{M \subseteq 2^{[n]} \mid |M|=k \}$ ... the goal is to design an algorithm to output the super-arm ${\tt Out} \in {\cal M}$ that satisfies ... $\Pr[\theta(M^*) - \theta({\tt Out}) \leq \varepsilon ] \geq 1-\delta$.

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial pure exploration (CPE) with general decision class, full-bandit feedback
unmapped: General decision class M (paths, matchings, matroids) of subsets of n base arms; only sum of rewards observed
Static allocation strategy p given as input
settings.definition_quote: Given any instance of CPE with a decision class ${\cal M}$ in the full-bandit setting

algorithms.name: SAQM (Static allocation algorithm with approximate quadratic maximization)
ICB (Static allocation with independent confidence bound)

conditions: noise bounded in [-R,R] (R treated as constant in main-text statement)
tuning: DkS-Oracle with best known approximation ratio (Bhaskara et al.) giving 1/alpha_t = O(k n^{1/8})

source.label: thm:topk
source.quote: Given any instance of the multiple-arm identification with full-bandit feedback, with probability at least $1-\delta$, {\tt SAQM} (Algorithm~\ref{alg:ECB}) returns an $\varepsilon$-optimal super-arm $\widehat{M}^*$ and the total number of samples $T$ is bounded as follows: T = O(k^2 H_eps (n^{1/4}k^3 log(n/delta) + log(n^{1/8} k^3 H_eps (n^{1/4} k^3 H_eps + log(n/delta))))).

results.notes: k mapped to m (super-arm size). Appendix proof version includes R factors (k^2 R^2 ...). Theorem number inferred from proof heading 'Proof of Theorem 3'. Per-round compute O(max{n^2, poly_DkS(n)}) (Theorem 2).

symbols.alpha_apx: approximation ratio of the CEM approximation algorithm

conditions: an alpha-approximation algorithm for CEM over the decision class is available

source.label: col:general
source.quote: Given any instance of CPE with a decision class ${\cal M}$ in the full-bandit setting, with probability at least $1- \delta$, {\tt SAQM} (Algorithm~\ref{alg:ECB}) with $\alpha$-approximation of CEM returns an $\varepsilon$-optimal set $\widehat{M}^*$, and the total number of samples $T$ is bounded as follows: T\leq 8(3+1/\alpha)^2 k^2 H_eps \log(c'K/\delta)+C(H_\varepsilon, \delta)

results.notes: First term is exact, second is O(.); recorded overall as O. R omitted as in statement.

symbols.H_eps_prime: rho'(p)/(Delta_min+epsilon)^2 with rho'(p) the squared max diagonal-approximation width

conditions: linear maximization over the decision class is polynomial-time solvable

source.label: thm:matroid
source.quote: Given any instance of combinatorial pure exploration with decision class $\cM$ in full-bandit setting, with probability at least $1- \delta$, {\tt ICB} (Algorithm~\ref{alg:ICB}) returns an $\varepsilon$-optimal super-arm $\widehat{M}^*$ and the total  number of samples $T$ is bounded as follows: T = O(k^2 H'_eps log(n/delta (k H'_eps (k^2 H'_eps + log(n/delta)))))

results.notes: Lemma number from 'Proof of Lemma 3' heading. Proof version includes R factors.
